item.title: Rebounding savant Oscar Tshiebwe finally gets NBA chance he’s deserved for years
item.description: Oscar Tschibwe set NCAA rebounding records while at Kentucky, yet he went undrafted in the 2023 NBA Draft. He finally got his shot this week with the Pacers.

item.title: Former Knicks guards Immanuel Quickley, RJ Barrett may yet prove Raptors won the OG Anunoby trade
item.description: The minute the OG Anunoby trade went down, Knicks fans all over were looking like that grimacing emoji, simultaneously excited but pensive about what had just happened.

item.title: Kobe Bufkin is balling out for Atlanta Hawks’ G League team. When will he be called up to NBA?
item.description: Atlanta Hawks rookie Kobe Bufkin probably didn't picture his first pro year going like this-- spent in mostly empty gymnasiums with pumped-in arena noise, playing against the likes of Luka Garza instead of Luka Doncic.

item.title: Why South Florida already deserves an NCAA Tournament bid
item.description: Despite having won 19 of 20 games and sitting at 14-1 in one of the best non-power conferences in the country, South Florida is in a tenuous spot when it comes to NCAA Tournament selection. Do they deserve it?

item.title: After long, seven-year road filled with excruciating losses, Celtics’ coast to NBA title felt ‘surreal’
item.description: When it was over, the Celtics were just too much for the Mavericks. Too many 3-point shooters to guard, too many athletic, wing defenders who could lock down Kyrie Irving and Luka Doncic, too many role players who knew exactly how to impact winning, and too much passion from the crowd, which exploded with every made 3 and Kyrie transgression.

item.title: What will we most remember these champion Boston Celtics for?
item.description: When the confetti is cleared from the court, the championship gear commercials stop playing and the dust settles on this tremendous season, what will we remember these Boston Celtics for?

item.title: Zach Edey posted an easy double-double in Summer League debut. Here’s why he’ll succeed in NBA
item.description: Zach Edey's going to succeed in the NBA. If you didn't already know this by watching the 7-4 big man dominate at Purdue, lifting the Boilermakers on his giant shoulders and carrying them to an NCAA title game appearance this spring, you should have seen it in his summer league debut on Monday night.

item.title: Paris Olympics takeaways: What did Team USA’s crunch-time lineup say about NBA’s hierarchy? O
item.description: It was fascinating to see who Steve Kerr trusted with everything on the line as the Americans trailed Serbia by 14 points in the semifinals entering the fourth quarter. The lineup he went with-- Steph Curry, Devin Booker, Kevin Durant, LeBron James and Joel Embiid-- is hard to argue with, even as Embiid ambled around on defense and allowed Serbia to get off open looks and to grab some key offensive rebounds.

item.title: Why Ange-in Spurs fans will back Postecoglou until bitter end
item.description: It's not just the expansive, daring, attacking style of football that draws Tottenham fans to Ange Postecoglou. It's something deeper than that-- his charisma.

item.title: Former Creighton standout Ryan Kalkbrenner making an early impact with Charlotte Hornets
item.description: If you remember watching Ryan Kalkbrenner at Creighton, you would have been forgiven for thinking the lanky, 7-foot Jim Parsons look-alike wouldn't have much of a shot in the NBA.
